purpose: Flucytosine is used to treat serious fungal infections in the body, especially infections caused by types of fungi called Candida and Cryptococcus. It is most commonly used to treat fungal infections of the blood, urinary tract, and brain (such as cryptococcal meningitis). It is almost always used together with another antifungal medicine, like amphotericin B, for best results.
how_it_works: Once you swallow flucytosine, your body absorbs it and it travels to where the fungal infection is. Fungal cells take it in and convert it into a substance that blocks the fungus from making the genetic material it needs to survive and grow. Basically, it stops the fungus from reproducing, allowing your immune system and the medication to clear the infection.
common_side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and stomach upset are common. You may also notice loss of appetite, headache, dizziness, or skin rash. Some people develop low blood cell counts, which can cause tiredness, easy bruising, or increased risk of infection.
warnings: This medication can be hard on your bone marrow, liver, and kidneys, so your doctor will monitor your blood counts and organ function closely with regular blood tests. Do not take this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as it can harm an unborn baby. Always take it exactly as prescribed and never skip doses, as the fungus can become resistant if levels in your body drop too low. Tell your doctor right away if you notice unusual bruising, bleeding, yellowing of skin or eyes, or signs of infection.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 25 mg per kilogram of your body weight taken by mouth every 6 hours (four times a day). Your doctor will adjust the dose based on your kidney function and blood levels of the drug. It is important to take each dose at evenly spaced times and with food to reduce stomach upset.
